record.nameMeaning: "Arm lizard", for its proportionately long forelimbs
record.oneLiner: A towering long-necked sauropod with longer arms than legs.
record.description: Brachiosaurus was a large sauropod with a disproportionately long neck, small skull, and — unusually — longer forelimbs than hindlimbs, giving it a steeply inclined trunk and a proportionally short tail. It lived in the Late Jurassic of North America and was a high browser, cropping vegetation up to about 9 m off the ground. Unlike other sauropods, it was unsuited to rearing on its hindlimbs.

discovery.where: Colorado River valley, western Colorado, USA

notableFacts.text: Unusually for a sauropod, its forelimbs were longer than its hindlimbs.
A high browser, cropping vegetation as high as ~9 m off the ground.
Most popular depictions are actually based on the African relative Giraffatitan.
